brief.title: The World's Most Valuable Companies in 2025
brief.one_liner: A comparative snapshot of the top 20 publicly traded companies by market capitalization, revealing the dominance of U.S. tech giants and the global spread across Taiwan, Saudi Arabia, South Korea, China, and the Netherlands.
brief.goal: The viewer should understand which companies lead the global economy by market value, how concentrated wealth is among the top tier, and how different countries and sectors are represented in the rankings.

sections.title: The Trillion-Dollar Club
sections.objective: Highlight the elite group of companies exceeding $1 trillion in market cap and show the massive gap between the top 5 and the rest.

sections.title: Country & Regional Dominance
sections.objective: Show how the U.S. dominates the top 20 list with 15 of 20 companies, and where other countries (Taiwan, Saudi Arabia, South Korea, China, Netherlands) appear.

sections.title: Sector Concentration
sections.objective: Illustrate that technology and semiconductor companies dominate the highest market cap positions, with finance and energy also represented.

sections.title: Putting It in Perspective
sections.objective: Contextualize the total market cap of the top 10 vs. the broader universe of nearly 11,000 tracked companies worth $143 trillion combined.
